context: Stress-tests not covered by codex's prior artifacts: partition robustness, convergence with N, subfamily invariance.

partition_robustness.method: Same orbit cache, different excursion partitions; 30k orbits, 1.06M canonical excursions.

every_step.note: matches Geom(2) closed-form Cramer rate 0.0542 to 3%

partition_robustness.headline_finding: J varies 30-80% with partition definition. The 'canonical' J=0.0837 is specific to tail-entry partition.
partition_robustness.implication: J is not a partition-independent universal constant.

convergence_with_N.method: Subsample canonical excursions to N_sub, recompute J.
convergence_with_N.headline_finding: J converges from N=20k upward; codex 1M sample is well-converged.

mersenne_like.headline_finding: J monotone decreasing with R, factor 2-3 smaller than aggregate. Reflects forced-a=1 positive drift in deep tails.

stratified_by_n0_mod_9.headline_finding: 3-adic structure essentially invariant (3% spread, within sampling).

calibrated_definition_of_J: J = 0.0837 is the Cramer rate of the Markov-renewal walk over accelerated Collatz orbits with tail-entry partition (excursion = run between consecutive n_t in 3 mod 4), evaluated over uniform odd n_0 in [10^4, 10^15]. It is partition-dependent and 2-adic-stratified; the partition-independent per-step rate has closed form ~0.0542 from the Geom(2) MGF.

candidate_for_universal_J_step.definition: Per-step Cramer rate = sup_lambda { log(2^(1+lambda) - 1) - lambda*log(3) }
candidate_for_universal_J_step.empirical_match: 0.0556 from per-step partition, 3% off closed form
candidate_for_universal_J_step.advantages: partition-independent, closed-form, matches Geom(2) heuristic, theoretically motivated

recommendation: Document J_renewal = 0.0837 as the Markov-renewal Cramer rate (specific partition), and J_step = 0.0542 as the partition-independent per-step Cramer rate (closed form via Geom(2) MGF). Stress-test data shows J_renewal is genuinely partition-dependent and 2-adic-stratified, while J_step is the universal sibling.
